summary: Fail. Review B audited the delta cb167393..0019518e at HEAD 0019518e (current) and found two Major defects in the new duplicate-key scanner. A duplicate key inside an array makes the gate hang (F9). A duplicate key written with an escape passes as a false pass (F10). A valid input of 100 MB aborts the gate with exit 134, where the previous gate gave exit 0 (F11, Minor). The cwd pin works. The live gate exits 0 from the repo root, from /tmp, from /, and from a directory with the base lockfile. The fail-closed harness gave 0 mismatches on 2238 inputs, the manifests are unchanged, and no secret, shell, or new dependency exists. A2 is not applicable. The plan claim at plan.md:21, that the scanner rejects any duplicate object key, is too wide (A6). One edit of hasDuplicateKeys fixes F9, F10, and F11. An in-memory prototype passed 9000 random documents.
blocking_findings: F9 [Major] review-b: The duplicate-key scanner never returns when a duplicate key sits in an object inside an array. scripts/audit-gate.mjs:130-133 sets `found` and returns from `readObject` in the middle of the object. The enclosing `readArray` loop (:113-120) then meets a `}` that `readValue` cannot consume, because `readPrimitive` (:105-109) stops at `}` without a step. The loop spins forever. Rationale: the document `{"metadata":{"vulnerabilities":{"info":0,"low":0,"moderate":0,"high":0,"critical":0}},"advisories":{},"x":[{"k":1,"k":2}]}` given with `--input` ran 8 s at 100% CPU and never exited (the `timeout` guard gave 124). The live path hung in the same way when `AUDIT_GATE_PNPM` named a stand-in that prints this text, because `TIMEOUT_MS` bounds only the child process. The values `[[{"k":1,"k":2}]]`, `[1,{"k":1,"k":2}]`, and `[{"k":1,"k":2,"z":3}]` for `x` also hang. A duplicate in a plain object, such as `{"x":{"k":1,"k":2}}`, exits 2 in 23 ms. In a first run of 3000 random valid documents, all 71 hanging documents held a raw duplicate. A second run of 9000 documents (3 seeds) hung on 218. A duplicate is the input that the gate must reject with exit 2, so the reject path must end. No false pass follows. `pnpm audit --json` cannot print a duplicate key (it uses JSON.stringify), so the exposure is a crafted `--input` file or a replaced `pnpm`. Disposition: Fix. Do not return early: set `found` to true and keep scanning, so the cursor stays in step. An in-memory prototype with this change gave 0 hangs on the same 9000 documents.

F10 [Major] review-b: A duplicate key written with an escape passes the scanner, so the gate gives a false pass. `readString` (scripts/audit-gate.mjs:87-104) returns each key with its escapes undecoded, and `readObject` (:129-134) stores that raw text in `seen`. JSON.parse decodes the keys and keeps the last value, so the two checks disagree. Rationale: the counts object holds `"high":3` and a later key. That key starts with the JSON escape for U+0068 (a backslash, then `u0068`), continues with `igh`, and has the value 0. The gate gave exit 0 and `critical=0 high=0 moderate=0 low=0 info=0`. The key `"critical":5` followed by a key that starts with the escape for U+0063 and the value 0 gave exit 0 and `critical=0`. The plain duplicate `"high":3,"high":0` gives exit 2. Four more pairs gave exit 0. Two are hex-case pairs: one letter, and one lone surrogate. Two use other escapes: a slash with its backslash escape, and an astral character with its surrogate-pair escape. The 9000-document run found 662 missed duplicates, all escape-only, and the first 3000-document run found 222. The plan claim at plan.md:21 that the scanner rejects `any duplicate object key` is therefore too wide (A6), and tests/fixtures/audit-duplicate-count-keys.json covers only the plain form. A caller needs control of the audit document to use this gap, so the exposure is small. The control exists to fail closed, and the brief names escapes as a probe. Disposition: Fix. Decode each key with `JSON.parse('"' + rawKey + '"')` before the `seen` check, then correct plan.md:21. An in-memory prototype with this change gave 0 missed duplicates and 0 false positives on the same 9000 documents.
nonblocking_findings: F11 [Minor] review-b: A valid input of about 100 MB aborts the gate with exit 134 and a V8 trace on stderr. The previous gate gave exit 0 on the same input. `readString` (scripts/audit-gate.mjs:87-104) builds each string one character at a time with `value += ch`. It does this for keys and for string values. The heap keeps about 32 bytes for each character. Rationale: a clean document with one 10 MB string used 538816 KB and 0.66 s. With 40 MB it used 1609376 KB and 3.37 s. With 100 MB the process stopped after 9.99 s at the 2 GB heap limit. It printed `FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit` and exited 134. The gate at cb167393 handled the same file in 0.32 s with 251964 KB and exit 0. The exit is not 0, so no false pass follows. The exit-2 contract and the `audit unavailable` only output are broken. The live path is safe, because `execFileSync` keeps its 1 MiB `maxBuffer` (round-2 probe, review-b-cb16739.json:18 and :36). Only `--input` is exposed. Disposition: Fix in the same edit as F9 and F10: take `text.slice(start, end)` for keys and do not build string values. An in-memory prototype gave exit 0 for the 100 MB file in 0.56 s with 260080 KB.

F4 [Nit] review-b (carried, unchanged): pnpm-lock.yaml still holds the pre-release packages `@emnapi/core@2.0.0-beta.2` and `@emnapi/runtime@2.0.0-beta.2` (pnpm-lock.yaml:75 and :81). The lockfile blob at 0019518e (bd1c5c22) equals the blobs at cb167393 and 1d00046d. plan.md records the decision to accept the packages (Accepted review notes, F4). Disposition: note; no action.

F7 [Nit] review-b (carried, unchanged): No test covers the timeout branch (`TIMEOUT_MS` at scripts/audit-gate.mjs:21, used at :178). plan.md records the decision to accept the gap (Accepted review notes, F7). F9 shows a related fact: `TIMEOUT_MS` bounds only the child process, and no timer bounds the gate's own parsing. Disposition: note; no action.

Fail-closed harness: 2238 inputs ran end to end, with one gate process for each input through --input on a /tmp file. The inputs came from 4 base documents: clean, high, critical, and moderate plus low. They hold every single-path mutation with 20 leaf values and with deletion. They also hold 17 severity strings at each advisory severity path, 300 seeded double mutations, and 22 raw texts. The raw texts include empty, truncated, BOM, trailing garbage, two documents, NaN, an error object, and a stdout warning. The exit tally was 527 times 0, 526 times 1, and 1185 times 2. An oracle that restates the plan.md contract gave 0 mismatches. It also found 0 hangs and 0 signals. Exit 2 never printed more than `audit unavailable` on stderr. Exit 0 and 1 never printed a different count line. These inputs hold no duplicate keys, so they test the unchanged logic. They give no proof for F9 and F10.

F9 and F10 end-to-end probes used the real gate, --input on a /tmp file, and an 8 s guard. The control clean document gave 0. The plain duplicate for high (3 then 0) gave 2 in 23 ms. Escape-spelled duplicates gave 0 for high, for critical, for hex case (U+00E9), for a slash, for a lone surrogate, and for an astral character. A raw astral duplicate and a raw e-acute duplicate gave 2. A precomposed e-acute against a decomposed e-acute gave 0. That result is correct, because JSON.parse also reads two keys. A duplicate inside an object in an array hung (guard 124) for `[{k,k}]`, `[{k,k,z}]`, `[[{k,k}]]`, and `[1,{k,k}]`. A duplicate inside `[{"y":{k,k}}]` gave 2, and a duplicate in a plain object gave 2.

Live hang: a stand-in pnpm script in /tmp printed the F9 document. AUDIT_GATE_PNPM=<stand-in> node scripts/audit-gate.mjs ran 8.007 s real and 7.997 s user. The 8 s guard ended it (exit 124). pgrep showed no leftover process.

Differential run: the real scanner function, cut from scripts/audit-gate.mjs, ran in a worker thread with an 80 ms watchdog for each document. An oracle decoded the keys and counted two keys as equal when the decoded strings were equal. The generator builds random valid JSON of depth 4. It uses arrays, objects, numbers, literals, and strings with braces, brackets, quotes, and escapes. Keys come from a pool of 20. Each key is written plain, fully escaped, or partly escaped, with mixed hex case and varied white space. Totals for 3 seeds (9000 documents): 7773 clean and accepted, 347 duplicates detected, 662 escape-only duplicates missed (false pass), 218 hangs, and 0 false positives. In the first run (3000 documents, one seed), 71 documents hung. In 57 of them the raw duplicate sat in an array element. In 14 it sat deeper, in an object inside an array. Every hanging document held a raw duplicate.

Deep nesting: a clean document plus an extra field n levels deep gave exit 0 for n up to 5000. It gave exit 2 with `audit unavailable` for n from 7000 to 1,000,000 (arrays 187 ms, objects 237 ms at 1,000,000). The recursive scanner overflows the stack near 6000 levels. The try/catch at scripts/audit-gate.mjs:194-198 turns the RangeError into exit 2. stderr held only `audit unavailable`. A raw duplicate at the bottom of 5000 and 20000 levels also gave exit 2. This fails closed.

Memory and time on large valid documents used heavy-run.sh, /usr/bin/time, and a guard of 150 s. A 10 MB string value took 0.66 s and 538816 KB. A 40 MB string value took 3.37 s and 1609376 KB. A 40 MB key took 3.31 s and 1543180 KB. 20 MB of escape pairs took 1.26 s and 751424 KB. A 20 MB array of numbers took 0.70 s and 192176 KB. 1,000,000 keys (11.3 MB) took 0.91 s and 327672 KB. A 100 MB string value aborted after 9.99 s with exit 134 (signal 6) and maxrss 2135220 KB. The gate at cb167393 (a copy of git show cb167393:scripts/audit-gate.mjs) read the 100 MB file in 0.32 s with 251964 KB and exit 0. My first run of the cb167393 gate read an empty piped script and printed no count line. I discarded it and re-ran from a file.

Prototype of the fix: hasDuplicateKeys with three changes, held in memory and in /tmp only. No repo file changed. The changes are: decode each key with JSON.parse before the seen check. Set found and keep scanning, with no early return. Take keys by slice and do not build string values. On the same 9000 documents it detected 1227 duplicates (347 plus 662 plus 218) and accepted 7773 clean documents. It missed 0, hung 0 times, and gave 0 false positives. End to end, all F9 and F10 probes gave 2 and the control gave 0. Two sibling objects with the same key gave 0, and the keys a and A gave 0. The 100 MB file gave exit 0 in 0.56 s with 260080 KB. The 40 MB key took 0.30 s and 219740 KB. I deleted the prototype files after the run. The prototype shows that a small fix exists. It does not replace Green's tests.

Static checks: scripts/audit-gate.mjs imports only node:child_process, node:fs, node:path, and node:url. The delta adds node:path and node:url. execFileSync gets the constant argument list ['audit', '--json'] and no shell option (:174-179). AUDIT_GATE_PNPM therefore names a program and nothing else. The script has no eval, no new Function, and no new dependency. A grep -inE over git diff cb167393..0019518e for secret patterns printed nothing (exit 1). The patterns were api key, secret, bearer, sk-, password, credential, authorization, _authToken, npm_, ghp_, github_pat_, AKIA, xox, private-key headers, and eyJ tokens. A scan of added lines for e-mail addresses and IPv4 addresses printed nothing.
A2: not applicable. git diff 7bc4a4e0..0019518e -- scripts tests src, piped to grep -inE 'published|draft|consent|anonymi', printed nothing (exit 1). No draft-to-published flip exists in the diff.

A6: no registry file claims that a security state is resolved. measure/tracks.md:20 lists the track as open ([ ]). measure/generated/status.md:26 shows status new with 0/3 tasks. plan.md:21 (T2 r4 evidence) says the scanner rejects `any duplicate object key` and that a duplicate exits 2. The adversarial test for this state is green only for the plain duplicate in tests/fixtures/audit-duplicate-count-keys.json.

Harness limits: three of my first attempts were invalid, and I discarded each one. (a) A shell probe of the escape case reached the gate as a plain duplicate, because the tool decoded the escape in my command text. I rebuilt every escape probe from String.fromCharCode(92). (b) The first differential run reported every document as a hang, because the worker thread inherited --input-type=module and failed to start. I set execArgv to an empty list and re-ran. (c) The cb167393 memory comparison is described above. The oracles restate the plan.md contract and the JSON.parse last-value rule. The runs prove conformance to that contract and the named defects. They do not prove that the contract is complete.
